A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisCoder2 work, with readable text, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The original case-study appendix F is retained as appendix G in v2; the new appendix F can be distinguished from retained material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VisPlotBench evaluations, training-data ablations, execution-error analyses, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds PandasPlotBench, HumanEval/HumanEval+, and quantitative training-corpus analyses.

M1.justification: The data-construction pipeline, Qwen2.5-Coder fine-tuning, and execution-feedback self-debug procedure remain unchanged. Appendix F.1 and Algorithm 1 document the existing correction loop rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds PandasPlotBench evaluations across Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly, plus HumanEval/HumanEval+ algorithmic programming tasks. This extends evaluation beyond v1's visualization-only coverage. The training corpus and original VisPlotBench tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Existing VisPlotBench comparator membership is unchanged. Table 23 newly includes VisCoder-14B with and without self-debug, extending the evaluated VisCoder baselines beyond v1's 3B/7B variants; otherwise, the added benchmarks reuse existing comparison families.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce HumanEval/HumanEval+ Pass@1 evaluation and library-specific PandasPlotBench comparisons at 3B, 7B, and 14B. Original training budgets, hyperparameters, and the three-round VisPlotBench correction limit remain unchanged; F.1 mainly supplies additional protocol documentation.

E4.justification: Appendix F.4 adds substantial corpus audits covering filtering and runtime failure rates, visualization-type diversity, and global/per-language instruction and code redundancy. Existing source ablations, error breakdowns, and case studies are retained; much of F.3 interprets existing evidence rather than adding new ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new failure and redundancy percentages are descriptive results, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 23–24 add external-benchmark results, and Tables 28–32 add corpus statistics, including 0.21% instruction and 3.03% code redundancy. Original results, including 82.4% overall execution at 32B with self-debug, remain unchanged. Some new summaries conflict with retained results: Table 25 gives GPT-4.1 final LilyPond execution as 65.5%, versus 63.6% in retained Table 12.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results, proofs, or substantive formal assumptions. The new pseudocode restates the existing evaluation procedure rather than adding mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and headline claims remain: a multilingual training corpus, VisPlotBench, and VisCoder2 outperforming open-source baselines and approaching proprietary performance. Abstract edits clarify corpus composition already explained in v1.

C2.justification: F.2–F.3 add interpretations concerning external-benchmark generalization and preservation of general coding ability. They substantially expand explanations of feedback informativeness, diminishing self-debug returns, unresolved failures, and language-dependent relationships between execution, task compliance, and visual quality.

D1.justification: F.1 adds pseudocode and details about stopping after successful correction and retaining outputs for evaluation. F.4 documents separate instruction/code normalization and SHA-1 duplicate detection. Existing training hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and resource-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to HumanEval, OpusAnimation, JanusCoder, and Agent Learning via Early Experience, and acknowledges HTML visualization work. The overall positioning around multilingual executable visualization and self-debug remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are preserved. Changes include localized abstract and limitations rewrites, appendix cross-references, author-role and conference-header edits, and insertion of appendix F before the renamed case-study appendix G.

P2.justification: v2 adds benchmark tables, corpus-audit tables, and an algorithm display. Tables 25–27 also reorganize selected existing self-debug results into compact summaries. Original figures and case-study displays are retained, with the latter relocated from appendix F to G.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmark evaluations and corpus audits improve empirical breadth and transparency beyond v1's VisPlotBench-only evaluation. These benefits are limited by conflicting repeated GPT rates in Tables 25–26 versus retained Tables 12–13, and by an overly confident interpretation of the HumanEval declines as evidence of preserved general coding ability. The additions provide useful evidence, but their reporting weaknesses limit the overall gain.
